clue.text: Wise man also in depression

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is placed inside the other here

parts.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A sage is also sunk in gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A pandit is a learned Hindu scholar, hence any wise or learned person.

clue.text: See 18
Not all fine sheets left to be tucked in where sleeping

indicators.note: being tucked in means these pieces go inside the trimmed word
not all of the word asks us to drop its final letter

parts.note: dandy means fine, excellent
a ream is a quantity of paper sheets

explanation.surface: Some fine bedsheets with the left side tucked in, ready for bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheets' looks like bedding but means paper; 'Not all' drops the tail of the adjective and 'to be tucked in' places the paper and left inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamland is the imaginary place one goes to in sleep, so it names where a sleeper is.

clue.text: Surprise found at the bottom of Uncle Sam's pants?

definitions.meaning: an unexpected event, as in a real ... for the books

definitions.text: found at the bottom of Uncle Sam's pants?
definitions.meaning: Americans call trousers pants, and the folded-up cuff at the bottom of a trouser leg is called by this name in Britain

explanation.surface: Something unexpected discovered at the bottom of an American's trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn-up is British slang for an unexpected event, and also a turned-back trouser hem.

clue.text: Wages doubled though homeless — it's said to be reassuring

indicators.note: doubled says the trimmed word is written out twice
homeless asks us to remove IN, the crossword's word for at home

parts.note: wages are a form of income

explanation.surface: Even with double pay but no home, someone says reassuring words.
explanation.walkthrough: IN means at home, so 'homeless' strips IN from INCOME, leaving COME, which is then doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of comfort or mild reproof, spoken to reassure someone.

clue.text: Become aware, fine old man of peace; conflict's ending, in fact

parts.note: to come to is to regain consciousness, becoming aware again
fine can mean thin, as in a fine thread
Kofi Annan, former UN Secretary-General and Nobel Peace Prize winner

indicators.note: ending picks out the last letter of the word conflict

explanation.surface: A peacemaker's realisation about the end of a conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: KOFI Annan headed the UN and shared the 2001 Nobel Peace Prize, hence 'old man of peace'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to introduce an afterthought, much like saying actually or in fact.

clue.text: An oxymoronic measure of lines?

parts.note: a unit of rhythm in verse whose name pairs a word from the decimal system with an imperial unit of length, which contradicts itself

explanation.surface: A self-contradictory way to measure lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot is the basic rhythmic unit of a line of poetry, such as an iamb.

clue.text: See 15
Doubted if spray damaged chassis, for instance

parts.note: mist is a fine spray of water
rusted describes metal damaged by corrosion, as a car chassis may be

explanation.surface: Someone was suspicious about whether spray had ruined a car's frame.
explanation.definitionFit: To mistrust is to doubt or be suspicious of, so mistrusted is a synonym of doubted.

clue.text: Forward thinker wants to cover Midlands city with wax?

indicators.note: covering puts the wax before the city in this across answer

parts.note: cere is an old word for wax, as in cerecloth
Brum is a nickname for Birmingham, a city in England's Midlands

explanation.surface: A forward-looking thinker hopes to coat Birmingham with wax.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUM is a nickname for Birmingham, a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebrum is the front part of the brain where thinking happens, so it is a forward thinker.

clue.text: Desire to see last of beetroot pickler

indicators.note: last of picks out the final letter of the word beetroot

parts.note: Damien Hirst, the artist famous for pickling a shark in formaldehyde

explanation.surface: Wanting to see the end of someone who pickles beetroot.
explanation.walkthrough: Damien HIRST is the British artist known for animals preserved in formaldehyde, so a 'pickler'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirst is a strong craving or longing, so it means desire.

clue.text: They're inclined to explore county without borders in state west of Queen's

indicators.note: west of puts the state before the Queen in this across answer
in tells us the trimmed county goes inside the state

parts.note: Maine is a US state

indicators.note: without borders means drop the first and last letters of the word county

parts.note: ER is the Queen's cipher (Elizabeth Regina), so Queen's gives ER plus S

explanation.surface: Explorers of slopes look at a county in a state lying west of the Queen's land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined' is the pun: climbers are drawn to slopes. 'Without borders' trims the county and 'west of' fixes the order; ER is the royal cipher of Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers explore slopes, so they are people inclined, in the sense of drawn to steep places.

clue.text: Fraudster investing pound in earthquake-damaged pub?

parts.note: Bam is the Iranian city devastated by an earthquake in 2003

indicators.note: investing means the pub surrounds the pound sign

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A con man puts money into a pub wrecked by an earthquake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earthquake-damaged' is not an anagram signal: BAM is the city in Iran destroyed by the 2003 earthquake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bamboozler is someone who cheats or tricks people, so a fraudster.

clue.text: Story an entertaining thing to pass round

indicators.note: passing round turns these pieces back the other way

parts.note: a gas is informal for something great fun

explanation.surface: A story is an amusing thing to circulate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To pass round' turns the whole two-piece phrase backwards; 'gas' as fun is informal, as in 'what a gas'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, originally an Old Norse tale.

clue.text: The bends around a river where the Chinese drink

indicators.note: around means the rearranged word surrounds the A
bends signals the word The is twisted into a new order

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: Divers' sickness strikes near a river where Chinese people drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bends' looks like divers' sickness, but 'bends' only twists the word The; 'around' wraps that round the A, and the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A teahouse is a café serving tea, especially in China or Japan.

clue.text: Merci? Has the Sûreté dealt with it?

definitions.text: Has the Sûreté dealt with it?

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: the second word rearranged under the first word as an anagram signal gives the clue word Merci

explanation.surface: A French thank-you, and a question about the French police.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as a cryptic instruction rearranges five letters into Merci; the Sûreté is the French detective police.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangland activity run by syndicates is the kind of thing a national detective force like the Sûreté investigates.

clue.text: US city where Shaw shot

parts.note: Sandie Shaw, the British 1960s pop singer
a go is a shot or attempt

explanation.surface: An American city where George Bernard Shaw took a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw suggests the playwright, but it is Sandie Shaw, British winner of Eurovision 1967.
explanation.definitionFit: San Diego is a large city in southern California.

clue.text: Such shooting practice curtailed by a Gulf state

parts.note: a bud is a new shoot on a plant

indicators.note: curtailed means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a habit is a practice or custom

explanation.surface: Gunfire practice is restricted by a Gulf state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' suggests guns but means a plant shooting, a BUD; 'curtailed' cuts HABIT to HABI, and the clue's last 'a' leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the largest emirate of the UAE, on the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Such is ill-defined, where the elderly congregate?

definitions.meaning: a matter that is unclear, not black and white

explanation.surface: A vague matter, or the place old folk gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is an issue without clear rules; grey hair makes it whimsically a region for older people.

clue.text: Pen striking last letter of passion, which was on the record

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: striking the last letter removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: lust is strong passion

explanation.surface: A writer crossing out the last letter of a passion that had been documented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like the definition but is the pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is the needle that sat in a vinyl record's groove, so it was on the record.

clue.text: Statesman with Koran to hand failing to grasp beginning of translation

indicators.note: grasping means the rearranged letters hold another letter
failing signals the words Koran to hand fall apart and are rearranged
beginning of picks out the first letter of the word translation

explanation.surface: A politician with a Koran nearby fails to understand the start of the translation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' scrambles KORANTOHAND, which 'to grasp' wraps round T, first of 'translation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from a US state is a statesman in a punning sense, here a native of that state.

clue.text: Such highs and lows raised in omnibus edition

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ups and downs lifted from a collected edition.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'raised' means read upwards, so the letters SEDIT run backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides rise and fall to high and low water, so they are highs and lows.

clue.text: See 6
Stapled gerund to obscure word

indicators.note: obscuring means the answer is concealed within the words Stapled gerund

explanation.surface: A grammar term fastened on to hide a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To give one's word is to make a promise, a solemn undertaking.

clue.text: The point is: if you've eaten enough, don't eat any more!

parts.note: having eaten enough, you are full
stop, cease eating

explanation.surface: Dietary advice: once you're satisfied, quit eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is the punctuation point that ends a sentence.

clue.text: Vacillating protects political hard-hitter

indicators.note: vacillating means wavering, so the letters of protects waver into a new order

explanation.surface: A wavering politician who still hits hard.
explanation.walkthrough: John PRESCOTT, the British deputy prime minister, punched an egg-throwing protester in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: John Prescott was a British Labour politician famous for punching a protester on the campaign trail.

clue.text: First of drugs put in place: ecstasy, then dope

indicators.note: put in means this letter goes inside the word for place

parts.note: a seat is a place to sit

indicators.note: First of picks out the initial letter of the word drugs

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug routine: something placed, ecstasy, then more dope.
explanation.definitionFit: To dope someone is to drug them, which is to sedate them.
